title: Noise-resilient and Scalable Quantum Error Correction for Nuclear Spin Qubits in Silicon with Electron Shuttling
authors: Wayne M. Witzel, Matthew D. Grace, Dwight R. Luhman
abstract: Nuclear spin qubits in silicon are well-isolated from their environment. Consequently, they have very long lifetimes and low sensitivity to noise, but this also suggests that control and measurement is challenging. We introduce electron pair interferometry (EPI), a protocol to overcome this challenge and maintain robustness to noise. EPI is implemented using an array of quantum dots with isoelectronic nuclear spin qubits located in the dots. A pair of electrons are initialized into a singlet ground state, split apart, and shuttled to the dots containing nuclear spin qubits. We show it is possible to coherently transfer the parity of the nuclei onto the measurable state of singlet/triplet-encoded electrons. Global nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) can be used to change bases and implement dynamical decoupling (DD). Combined with selective hyperfine-induced $Z_π$ rotations, our gate set is complete for universal quantum computation, tailored to Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum error correction, and robust to noise. We discuss very low sensitivity to charge noise and study the sensitivity to both DC and AC magnetic field inhomogeneity which depends strongly on their relative strengths.
summary: This work presents a method to enable quantum computation using nuclear spin qubits in silicon by employing Electron Pair Interferometry (EPI) mediated by electron shuttling. This technique allows for robust measurement of nuclear spin parity, which is then integrated into a full error correction cycle using global NMR gates. The result is a scalable and noise-resilient protocol for universal quantum computation.
main_problem: The challenge of controlling and measuring nuclear spin qubits in silicon due to their long coherence times, which results in low sensitivity to external control signals.
main_result: A complete gate set for universal quantum computation is achieved by combining Electron Pair Interferometry (EPI) with global NMR techniques, providing a noise-resilient framework tailored for CSS quantum error correction.
method: The core method involves using electron pair interferometry (EPI) to coherently transfer the parity of nuclear spins onto measurable electron states, which is then integrated into a full syndrome extraction cycle using global NMR gates.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an array of nuclear spin qubits embedded in silicon quantum dots. Control relies on shuttling pairs of electrons initialized in a singlet state to mediate parity measurements via hyperfine interactions.
key_observables: Parity of the nuclear spins (measured via Singlet/Triplet electron states), fidelity of CPhase gates, and syndrome detection outcomes for CSS codes.
important_parameters: Hyperfine interaction strengths ($\sim 100$ kHz to $400$ kHz), coherence times ($T_2$), and relative strengths of DC vs. AC magnetic field inhomogeneities.
main_assumptions: The process requires adiabatic shuttling during EPI, and the analysis assumes static (perfectly correlated) magnetic field inhomogeneity for error modeling.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the global NMR cycle for syndrome extraction and achieving universality; Figure 2 details the Detector Error Model (DEM) under various magnetic field inhomogeneity scenarios with/without Dynamical Decoupling.
paper_structure: The paper introduces EPI to measure nuclear parity, details how this measurement is integrated into a full quantum error correction cycle using global NMR gates, and concludes by demonstrating that the combined set achieves universal computation robustly against noise sources like charge noise.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, solid-state realization pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computing by engineering complex interactions (electron shuttling) to overcome intrinsic qubit limitations (long coherence times).
